subject: Logic
title: No Quintic Formula
description: A micro-lesson that makes No Quintic Formula usable.

hook.text: Quadratic equations have a formula. Cubics and quartics do too. But degree five? Abel proved: no formula exists.

buildup.text: For centuries, algebraists searched for a general formula to solve fifth-degree polynomials using basic operations.

discovery.text: Niels Henrik Abel proved in 1824 that no such formula can exist—it's not undiscovered, it's impossible.

twist.text: Galois later showed why: the symmetry group of quintics is too complex to be broken down by radicals.

climax.text: Both proved it in their twenties. Both died young. Their work founded modern algebra and group theory.

punchline.text: Some equations refuse to be solved by formula.

quiz.question: What did Abel prove about fifth-degree equations?
options: No general formula using radicals can solve them
